summary: Naṭīḥah refers to an animal, often a sheep or goat, that has been killed by being gored by another animal's horn, making its meat unlawful to eat.
lane: نَطِيحٌ ذ Smitten with the horn and so killed: fem. with ة : (L, K:) pl. نَطْحَى (L) and نَطَائِحُ : (Lh, L:) you say also نَعْجَةٌ نَطِيحٌ , as well as نطيحة . (L.) -b2- Also نَطِيحَةٌ A sheep or goat (Az) smitten with the horn and so killed. (Az, S,) and of which the flesh is therefore unlawful to be eaten: (Az:) the ة is added because it is made a subst., not an epithet: (Az:) or because the quality of a subst. predominates in it, as in the case of فَرِيسَةٌ and أَكِيلَةٌ and رَمِيَّةٌ . (S.) -b3- نَطِيحٌ and (tropical:) What comes to thee from before thee, (or faces thee, L,) of birds and wild animals (S, L, K) &c., which one rouses by throwing a stone or by crying out, and from the course of which one augurs evil or good: (L:) contr. of قَعِيدٌ . (S.) [The نطيح or is of evil omen.] -b4- Hence, (TA,) نَطِيحٌ (tropical:) An unfortunate, or unlucky, man. (K.) -b5- نَطِيحٌ A horse having a blaze, or white mark on his face, extending to one of his ears, which is deemed unlucky: (L:) or a horse having on his forehead two circular or spiral curls of hair ( دَائِرَتَانِ ), which are disliked: (S, L, K:) if there be but one, it is called دَائِرَةُ اللَّطَاةِ ; and this is not disliked; (S;) or it is called لَطْمَةٌ ; and the horse, لَطِيمٌ . (L.)

headwords.def: aor. نَطِحَ and نَطَحَ, (S, K,) inf. n. نَطْحٌ, (S,) He (a ram, S, L, and the like, L) smote him with his horn. (K.) مَا نَطَحَتْ فِيهِ جَمَّآءَ َاتُ قَرْنٍ [ A horned animal did not smite with its horn for him a hornless ewe ]: a proverb, said of him who has perished unavenged. (L.) [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii. 507.] نَطَحَهُ عَنْهُ (tropical:) He pushed him, or thrust him, away from him, and removed him. (A.)

inf. n. نِطَاحٌ (L, Msb) and مُنَاطَحَةٌ, (Msb,) They two (rams or he-goats) smote each other with their horns. (L.) بَيْنَهُمَا نِطَاحٌ (tropical:) [ Between them two is a contention like that of two rams ]; said of two learned men, and of two merchants. (A.) جَرَى لَنَا فِى السُّوقِ نِطَاحٌ (tropical:) [ There happened to us in the market a contention like that of two rams ]. (A.) [ نَاطَحَهُ He, or it, faced, or was or came opposite to him, or it ]: نِطَاحٌ is syn.
تَنَاْطَحَ see 8. تَنَاطَحَتِ الأَمْوَاجُ, and السُّيُولُ, (tropical:) [ The waves, and the torrents, conflicted, or dashed together. ] (A.)

انتطحتِ الكِبَاشُ , and, (S, K,) The rams smote one another with their horns. (K.) لَا يَنْطِحُ فِيهَا عَنْزَانِ [ Two she-goats will not, in it, smite each other with their horns ]: i. e., two weak persons will not encounter each other in it: alluding to a case in which there will not happen any discord or contention. (L, from a trad.)

Smitten with the horn and so killed: fem. with ة: (L, K:) pl. نَطْحَى (L) and نَطَائِحُ: (Lh, L:) you say also نَعْجَةٌ نَطِيحٌ, as well as نطيحة. (L.) Also نَطِيحَةٌ A sheep or goat (Az) smitten with the horn and so killed. (Az, S,) and of which the flesh is therefore unlawful to be eaten: (Az:) the ة is added because it is made a subst., not an epithet: (Az:) or because the quality of a subst. predominates in it, as in the case of فَرِيسَةٌ and أَكِيلَةٌ and رَمِيَّةٌ.

كَبْشٌ نَطَّاحٌ [ A ram that smites much with his horn ]: (S:) and [signifies the same: and] is applied to a man [app. as meaning who pushes, thrusts, or repels, much, or vehemently ]. (IAar, TA in art. ردس.)

دَائِرَةُ النَّاطِحِ A certain circular or spiral curl of hair on a horse, which is deemed unlucky. (L.) [See نَطِيحٌ.] نَاطِحٌ (tropical:) A difficulty; a distressing event; an affliction; a calamity: pl. نَوَاطِحُ. (S, K.) Ex. أَصَابَهُ نَاطِحٌ A difficulty, or distressing event, befell him. (S.) نَوَاطِحُ الدَّهْرِ The difficulties, &c., of fortune. (S.) النَّطْحُ وَالنَّاطِحُ (tropical:) [ The two stars called ] الشَّرَطَانِ, [q.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
